articles.headline: Ex-NBA champ JR Smith arrested on assault charge in Texas
articles.description: Former NBA champion JR Smith was arrested Monday in Texas on a charge of assault causing "bodily injury family violence."
articles.body:
Former NBA champion JR Smith was arrested Monday in Texas on a charge of assault causing "bodily injury family violence," according to jail records.

Smith, 41, was booked into Hunt County Detention Center on Monday after being arrested by the Royse City Police Department. No bond has been set, and Smith apparently remained in jail as of midday Tuesday, according to jail records.

Smith's representatives did not immediately respond to an ESPN message requesting comment.

The Royse City Police Department received an alert indicating the Southlake Police Department had issued a warrant for Smith, according to a release from Kirk Aldridge, the Royse City chief of police. Smith's license plate was spotted on Interstate 30, northeast of Dallas. Officers identified Smith and arrested him.

Smith was driving with his brother, Aldridge stated. Police released the car to Smith's brother when they arrested Smith.

In a news release Tuesday, Southlake police called Smith's arrest part of an "ongoing investigation." The police department declined to provide further information. 

According to a Southlake police spokesperson, Smith will be arraigned in Tarrant County.

Southlake is northwest of Dallas.

In 2009, Smith was sentenced to 90 days in jail -- with 60 days suspended -- and 500 hours of community service for reckless driving after causing a car accident that killed one of his friends in 2007. Smith expressed remorse, telling the court in 2009 that "it's been unbearable to deal with. I'm deeply sorry," The Associated Press reported at the time.

Smith played 16 seasons in the NBA for New Orleans Hornets, Denver Nuggets, New York Knicks, Cleveland Cavaliers and Los Angeles Lakers. He last played a game in 2020 with the Lakers and averaged 12.4 points, 3.1 rebounds and 2.1 assists during his career.

He won two NBA championships as a player and was named the NBA Sixth Man of the Year in 2013. After his NBA career, Smith played college golf for North Carolina A&T. He graduated from the school in May.

articles.headline: Man City owners inflated revenue by £830m - Premier League breaches findings
articles.description: Manchester City's owners artificially inflated the club's commercial revenue by £830 million between 2009 and 2018, the Independent Commission found during the Premier League hearing into the 115 charges for serious financial breaches.
articles.body:
Manchester City's owners artificially inflated the club's commercial revenue by £830 million ($1.08 bn) between 2009 and 2018, the Independent Commission found during the Premier League hearing into the 115 charges for serious financial breaches.

The Abu Dhabi-owned club were found guilty of all charges by the Commission with Premier League CEO Richard Masters saying City "systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade."

And in the written findings explaining the Commission's verdict, City were found guilty of using a Disguised Funding Scheme which enabled the club's owners to grossly inflate the real commercial earnings by directly funding the team.

During the 2017-18 season, Pep Guardiola's second in charge of the team, City recorded £145.73 million ($192.4m) in commercial revenue, with only £11 million ($14.5m) paid by sponsors and the remaining £134.73 million ($178m) paid by the owners, which is against Premier League rules.

Between 2009 and 2018, City declared a total of £949.94 million ($1.25 billion) in commercial revenue from Abu Dhabi sponsors, but only £119.25 million ($157m) of that figure was paid for by the sponsors.

- Man City learned of guilty verdicts in summer before transfer activity - sources

- Pochettino says no punishment can repair Manchester City damage

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

A total of £830.39 million ($1.08 bn) in so-called Tagged Sums were paid to the club by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) the vehicle used by Abu Dhabi as the club's owners.

During that nine-year period, City won three Premier League titles and signed several star players including Carlos Tevez, Sergio Aguero, Kevin De Bruyne and David Silva as well as hiring Guardiola as manager in 2016.

Further evidence showed that a £9.9m ($13.m) "hole" in the club's accounts was "plugged" to avoid a failure to comply with regulations in 2012-13.

"In a matter of days, without AD [Abu Dhabi] Sponsors even being approached, a number of modified AD Sponsor Agreements were generated which purported to reflect 'agreements' on the part of certain AD Sponsors to increase recorded Sponsorship Fees per se, to pay bonuses for events that had already taken place and to pay for a US tour," the written findings said.

articles.headline: Falcons' Tua Tagovailoa healing, embracing backup QB role
articles.description: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa says he's not 100% recovered from his oblique injury but is embracing his role as backup to Michael Penix Jr.
articles.body:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. - Tua Tagovailoa is taking his role as the current backup quarterback for the Atlanta Falcons in stride.

Michael Penix Jr. has positioned himself firmly as the team's starter after an impressive comeback performance last Thursday night in a 35-14 win over the Green Bay Packers. Tagovailoa said he will try to support Penix as much as he can.

"You've got to do everything you can to make sure you're not the reason he's failing," Tagovailoa said Tuesday. "So, that's where I look at my job being right now for Mike and whatever he needs in terms of off-the-field film, extra throws, questions, whatever it is, whatever that looks like. That's what my job description entails right now."

Tagovailoa was named the Week 1 starter out of training camp with Penix still working his way back from November left ACL surgery. But then Tagovailoa injured his oblique during Week 1. In practice on Sept. 10, he grabbed at his side and sat on the grass, clearly in discomfort. He was ruled out the next day and Cooper Rush, Atlanta's third-string quarterback, started the team's first two games, both losses.

Tagovailoa said he actually first felt the pain the day before and tried to work through it.

"Just thought it wasn't something as serious, just man, maybe my back or something might have locked up," Tagovailoa said. "But that's what it was (an oblique) and it's unfortunate, but it is what it is."

Tagovailoa said he's doing much better now, though maybe not completely 100%. He was off the injury report last week and active as the backup.

Tagovailoa was released by the Miami Dolphins during the offseason after a league-high 15 interceptions in 2025. The Dolphins took on a record $99.2 million to part ways with him. The Falcons signed him for one year and $1.3 million to compete with Penix for the starting job.

If Tagovailoa does get a start this season, it will only be the third time since 1991 that one team has started two left-handed quarterbacks in the same season.

"I'm always going to look at it as a competition," Tagovailoa said. "But as I said, this is the job description right now. Mike's the guy. We have to do everything we can to support him and we're going to support him."

articles.headline: Man City's guilt the talk of the town around English football
articles.description: The news that Man City were found guilty of all charges by the Premier League was the only topic of conversation around Manchester, and lower-league games, over the weekend.
articles.body:
STOCKPORT, England -- On the brisk approach to Edgeley Park on Saturday afternoon, the topic of conversation among the football fans streaming towards the stadium was not Stockport County or their visitors, Peterborough United. It wasn't the state of the League One table, or how England would get on against Spain later the same day either.

All anyone was talking about was Manchester City.

At one point during the second half of Stockport's 1-0 win, the loudest group of home supporters at the top of the Cheadle End behind one of the goals began singing "City's going down with a billion in the bank." It's a song City fans have often used about themselves in jest, but it's taken on new meaning in the aftermath of news Friday that the club have been found guilty of more than 100 breaches of financial rules.

News then broke on Tuesday with the full scope of the Premier League's guilty verdict against City, with sources also telling ESPN that the club was made aware of the findings over the summer, prior to their aggressive spending in the transfer window.

There was a time when Stockport and City -- clubs separated by just 10 miles -- were genuine rivals. They played each other six times in the league between 1997 and 2002. Stockport lost only once in those head-to-head encounters, but in 2009, they entered administration and were hit with a points deduction. It was the starting gun for a drop through the English football pyramid, a journey that bottomed out in the sixth tier.

It's a fate that could now await City. In the absence of anything official from the independent commission tasked with sorting through the Premier League's case, the void of information is being filled with guesswork and Manchester is at the centre of the storm.

On Sunday in east Manchester, hundreds of children turned up at Wright Robinson College to play junior matches. The walk from the carpark to the pitches is a long one and discussions filling the time -- between eight-year-olds and 18-year-olds alike -- were all about what might happen to one of the city's biggest clubs.

Amid the mild teasing of City fans, there were debates about whether Manchester United should be awarded the 2012 Premier League title and if Erling Haaland could end up playing in League Two. One City-supporting parent joked that the amount of memes and WhatsApp messages he'd received over the weekend had forced him to draft his own media statement as a catch-all response to each ping of his phone.

There have been two official statements from City -- one from the club on Friday afternoon, and another from chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak 24 hours later -- but little in the way of tangible information. Haaland was pulled out of a Norway news conference on Saturday for that reason. The charges and their impact would have dominated and no one -- let alone Haaland -- has any real answers.

articles.headline: Super Bowl LXI odds: All 32 teams' odds to win the championship
articles.description: Every NFL team's win total, as well as odds to win their division, the conference and Super Bowl LXI.
articles.body:
For the first time since the NFL season began, the Los Angeles Rams are not the standalone favorites to win Super Bowl LXI. After their second loss of the season, the Rams lengthened to +670, up from the +500 they had coming into the campaign, to tie them with the 3-0 Buffalo Bills, who have improved from the second-best 10-1 they entered the season at.

Next on the odds board is another tie between the Baltimore Ravens and San Francisco 49ers at +900. The former has improved from 10-1 at the beginning of the season, but the latter has made a big jump from 19-1 after an impressive undefeated start to the campaign. San Francisco is also tied with Los Angeles for the best odds to win the NFC at +400. The reigning champion Seattle Seahawks (10-1) and Kansas City Chiefs (+1050) round out the top six.

One of the most compelling divisions in the young season has been the NFC North, and Week 3's results had a big effect on team futures. The Detroit Lions continue to have the division's best Super Bowl odds at 19-1, but the Chicago Bears and Minnesota Vikings are quickly making up ground, both at 24-1. Meanwhile, the Green Bay Packers have taken a big hit in the future odds after a rocky 1-2 start, showing 55-1 after three weeks... a significant lengthening from 25-1 a week prior.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

articles.headline: Man City guilty of all charges of Premier League financial breaches
articles.description: Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations, the Premier League confirmed in a 1,545-word statement Tuesday.
articles.body:
Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations, the Premier League confirmed in a 1,545-word statement Tuesday.

Richard Masters, the Premier League CEO, said that the findings show that City "systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade."

City face huge points deductions and fines, with the Premier League holding the ability to issue an ultimate sanction of expulsion from the league.

City, who denied all charges, have until Friday to exercise their right to an appeal.

In its verdict, the independent panel found that City arranged "sham" contracts with commercial partners to artificially inflate their commercial earnings, filed "misstated" accounts to conceal the true nature of their finances and "significantly" breached Premier League and UEFA spending limits.

In its statement, the Premier League said City used "disguised funding schemes" to deceive and mislead the league.

The statement said: "The purpose of these schemes was found to have been to artificially inflate the club's revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than £900 million during the affected period, to appear to comply with financial rules.

"The consequence of this, as the Commission found, was that the club filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators. The Commission concluded that 'by its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the PL Rules.'"

Masters, who has been criticized for the length of time taken to bring City to account, said the verdict was a "vindication" of the decision to take action against the club.

"The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period," Masters said. "It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

"It also vindicates the Premier League's decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

- Man City learned of guilty verdicts in summer before transfer activity - sources

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Pochettino says no punishment can repair Manchester City damage

"It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition.

"It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

"This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches.

articles.headline: Expected fantasy points (xFP): 2026 leaderboard for TEs
articles.description: xFP focuses solely on opportunity. Here are the leaders for 2026.
articles.body:
Expected fantasy points (xFP) strips away player talent and efficiency and focuses solely on opportunity.

FORP -- fantasy points over replacement player -- is the difference between a player's actual fantasy point total (FF points) and his xFP (or expected total).

Tight end adjustments are made as follows:

Rushing attempts: No change

Rushing yardage: Rush attempts multiplied by a rusher's expected yardage based on position and rush direction

Rushing touchdowns: Rushing xTD

Targets: No change

Receptions: Targets multiplied by a receiver's expected catch rate based on depth of throw, location and position

Receiving yardage: Targets multiplied by a receiver's expected yardage based on depth of throw, location and position

Receiving touchdowns: Receiving xTD

Two-point conversions: xTD multiplied by the league average 2-point rate

Fumbles lost: Touches multiplied by the league average rate

Return touchdowns: Excluded due to extreme rareness and randomness
